text:
A spaceship in space sweeps stationary
interplanetary dust. As a result, its mass

increases at a rate $\frac{dM(t)}{dt}$ $= bv^{2}(t)$, where v(t) is
its instantaneous velocity. The instantaneous
acceleration of the satellite is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $\frac{dM(t)}{dt}$ $= bv^{2}(t)$

In free space
no external force
so there is only thrust force on rocket.

$F_{$thrust} = v$\frac{dm}{dt}$

Force on satellite = $-\vec{v}\frac{dm(t)}{dt}$

$M(t)a = – v (bv^{2})$

$\Rightarrow$ a = $-\frac{bv^{3}}{M(t)}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot

text:
A ring is hung on a nail. It can oscillate, without
slipping or sliding 
(i) in its plane with a time
period $T_{1}$ and, 
(ii) back and forth in a direction
perpendicular to its plane, 
with a period $T_{2}$. The
ratio $\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}$ will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Moment of inertia in case (i) is $I_{1}$

Moment of inertia in case (ii) is $I_{2}$

$I_{1} = 2MR^{2}$

$I_{2} =$ $\frac{1}{2}MR^{2}$ $+ MR^{2} =$ $\frac{3}{2}MR^{2}$

$T_{1} =$ $2π\sqrt{\frac{I_{1}}{Mgd}}$

and $T_{2} =$ $2π\sqrt{\frac{I_{2}}{Mgd}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{I_{1}}{I_{2}}}$

= $\sqrt{\frac{2MR^{2}}{\frac{3}{2}MR^{2}}}$

= $\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot

text:
In an adiabatic process, the density of a
diatomic gas becomes 32 times its initial value.
The final pressure of the gas is found to be n
times the initial pressure. The value of n is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In adiabatic process

$PV^{γ} =$ constant

$\Rightarrow$ $P\left (\frac{m}{ρ}\right )^{γ}$ = constant

As mass is constant

$\therefore$ P $\propto$ $ρ^{γ}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{P_{f}}{P_{i}}=\left (\frac{ρ_{f}}{ρ_{i}}\right )^{γ}$ = $(32)^{\frac{7}{5}}$ $= 2^{7} = 128$

[ For diatomic gas $γ$ = $\frac{7}{5}$ ]
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot

text:
A parallel plate capacitor has plate of length
'l', width ‘w’ and separation of plates is ‘d’. It
is connected to a battery of emf V. A dielectric
slab of the same thickness ‘d’ and of dielectric
constant k = 4 is being inserted between the
plates of the capacitor. At what length of the
slab inside plates, will the energy stored in the
capacitor be two times the initial energy
stored?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$C_{i} =$ $\frac{ε_{0}A}{d}=\frac{ε_{0}lw}{d}$

$U_{i} =$ $\frac{1}{2}C_{i}V^{2}$ = $\frac{1}{2}\frac{ε_{0}lw}{d}V^{2}$

[IMG]


$C_{f}$
 $= C_{1} + C_{2}$

= $\frac{Kε_{0}A_{1}}{d}+\frac{ε_{0}A_{2}}{d}$

= $\frac{Kε_{0}wx}{d}+\frac{ε_{0}w(l-x)}{d}$

= $\frac{ε_{0}w}{d}[Kx+l-x]$

$\therefore$ $U_{f} =$ $\frac{1}{2}C_{f}V^{2}$

= $\frac{1}{2}\frac{ε_{0}w}{d}[Kx+l-x]V^{2}$

Given $U_{f}$
 $= 2U_{i}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{2}\frac{ε_{0}w}{d}[Kx+l-x]V^{2}$ = 2 $\times$ $\frac{1}{2}\frac{ε_{0}lw}{d}V^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ kx + l – x = 2l

$\Rightarrow$ 4x – x = l

$\Rightarrow$ 3x = l

$\Rightarrow$ x = $\frac{l}{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot

text:
The acceleration due to gravity on the earth’s
surface at the poles is g and angular velocity of
the earth about the axis passing through the
pole is $ω$. An object is weighed at the equator
and at a height h above the poles by using a
spring balance. If the weights are found to be
same, then h is (h << R, where R is the radius
of the earth)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At equator, $g_{1} = g - Rω^{2}$

At height $h, g_{2} =$ $g\left (1-\frac{2h}{R}\right )$ [as given h << R]

$\because$ Weight same at equator and at height h above the pole (so $g_{1}$
 $= g_{2})$

$\therefore$ g - R$ω^{2}$ = $g\left (1-\frac{2h}{R}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $Rω^{2}=\frac{2gh}{R}$

$\Rightarrow$ $h=\frac{R^{2}ω^{2}}{2g}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot

text:
Two coherent sources of sound, $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$,
produce sound waves of the same wavelength,
$λ$ = 1 m, in phase. $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ are placed 1.5 m
apart (see fig). A listener, located at L, directly
in front of $S_{2}$ finds that the intensity is at a
minimum
 when he is 2 m away from $S_{2}$. The
listener moves away from $S_{1}$, keeping his
distance from $S_{2}$ fixed. The adjacent maximum
of intensity is observed when the listener is at
a distance d from $S_{1}$. Then, d is :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Initially $S_{2}L = 2 m$

$S_{1}L =$ $\sqrt{2^{2}+(1.5)^{2}}$ = 2.5 m

For minimum at (L)

$S_{1}L – S_{2}L =$ $\Delta$x = $(2n+1)\frac{λ}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 2.5 - 2 = $(2n+1)\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 0.5 = $\frac{(2n+1)}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 1 = 2n + 1

$\Rightarrow$ n = 0 (first minima)

so at P $\to$ first maxima

$\therefore$ $S_{1}P – S_{2}P = nλ$ = 1$λ$

$\Rightarrow$ d - 2 = 1

$\Rightarrow$ d = 3 m

text:
A body of mass 2 kg is driven by an engine
delivering a constant power of 1 J/s. The body
starts from rest and moves in a straight line.
After 9 seconds, the body has moved a
distance (in $m) _______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let s be the required distance.


[IMG]


From Work - Energy theorem,

Work = Change in kinetic energy

$\Rightarrow$ Power $\times$ Time = $\Delta$K

i.e., Pt = $\Delta$K $\Rightarrow$ Pt = $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2} ..... (i)$

Given, $P = 1 Js^{-1}, t = 9 s, m = 2 kg$

Substituting all the given values in eq. (i), we get

1 $\times$ 9 = $\frac{1}{2}(2) v^{2}$

$v^{2} = 9$ $\Rightarrow$ v = 3 m/s (at t = 9 s)

As, Fv = P $\Rightarrow$ (ma)v = P [$\because$ F = ma]

$\Rightarrow m\left [\frac{dv}{dt}\right ]v=P\Rightarrow m\left [\frac{ds}{dt}\frac{dv}{ds}\right ]v=P$

$\Rightarrow m\left [v\frac{dv}{ds}\right ]v=P$

$\Rightarrow 2v^{2}dv=ds$ {$\because$ P = 1 J/s and m = 2 kg}

Integrating both sides,

$\int\limits _{0}^{3}2v^{2}dv=\int\limits _{0}^{s}ds\Rightarrow \frac{2}{3}[v^{3}]_{0}^{3}=s$

$\frac{2}{3}[27-0]=s\Rightarrow s=18$ m

Hence, after 9 s, the body has moved a distance of 18 m.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot
